author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays in the existing vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure, feature-package ADR) and uses only In-force catalog patterns (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog). The adjustment has three parts. A SpecialtyRepository follows the PetTypeRepository precedent. Without it the unheld specialties of edge case 1 cannot be listed, because VetRepository only sees held specialties. A SpecialtyDirectory value object computes the inversion, so the web controller stays free of rules (Web controller row; testing-principles pyramid: the grouping can be tested without booting the framework). A thin SpecialtyController serves GET /specialties.html with view vets/specialtyList. Design writes: three new Contracts rows plus REQ-VET-003 on Vet, Specialty, VetRepository; the vet line in Package Structure; a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-directory row. No ADR: the choice is contained in this slice. Oracle not connected; covering symbols resolved by reading src/main/java/.../vet/*.java and fragments/layout.html (weaker basis than symbol lookup).
integration_points: Binding: GET /specialties.html binds nothing. It takes no request parameter, path variable, or form object, so no @InitBinder and no allow-list is needed (security-principles § Trust Boundaries)

Repository boundary in SpecialtyDirectoryTests: none. The tests are plain unit tests over real Vet and Specialty instances built through a test factory (testing-principles § data construction; Mocking Policy: never mock internal code)

Repository boundary in SpecialtyControllerTests (@WebMvcTest, MockMvc as the sanctioned transport double): hand-written doubles of SpecialtyRepository and VetRepository, registered as beans. A @MockitoBean stub is not sanctioned here (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: a hand-written double fits both one-method interfaces)
SpecialtyController reads SpecialtyRepository.findAll and the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(), builds a SpecialtyDirectory, and puts it on the model

Template vets/specialtyList.html uses fragments/layout with a menu value matching no nav entry, so it carries shared navigation (REQ-SYS-001) without highlighting or adding an entry. Holder names and specialty names render through th:text, never th:utext (system-design § Threat Model, XSS row)
Message keys: reuse the existing keys (specialties, vets, name) where they fit. Any new key lands in every bundle under src/main/resources/messages/ (REQ-LANG-002 bundle-parity test)

patterns.description: package-private controller with constructor-injected repository; the new controller follows it without pagination
layout fragment use and first-then-last full-name rendering; in this slice SpecialtyDirectory composes the full name

risks.risk: Holders matched to specialties by object reference. The two reads run in separate persistence contexts and the vet read is cached, so the Specialty instances differ and every specialty shows no holders
risks.mitigation: Group by the specialty's identity (BaseEntity id) inside SpecialtyDirectory. Specialty declares no equals (architecture-principles § Scoped exception: entities keep framework identity). A unit test with distinct instances sharing an id pins it

risks.risk: Specialty directory path scales with specialties and vet-specialty pairs (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-directory row)
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: two whole-collection reads and one keyed pass; no pagination, no extra query per specialty

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory exposes the mutable entities it was built from, which breaks the value-object closed properties (architecture-principles § Scoped exception: does not cover a value object)
risks.mitigation: Make it a record holding unmodifiable lists of the specialty's stored name and holders' full-name strings, copied at construction

risks.risk: Tests assert an order the requirement does not set (prd Open Questions: no order for REQ-VET-003)
risks.mitigation: Assert membership only, never order, for specialties and for holders

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Narrow readings taken where the request leaves a choice open: the page reuses the shared layout but passes a menu value that activates no nav entry; an unheld specialty renders its name with an empty holder list and no 'none' wording, per the PRD Open Questions. The value-object name SpecialtyDirectory follows the PRD wording. Open Question 5 (vet cache with no eviction) is unchanged: the new specialty read is uncached.

blast_radius.note: All production changes are new files in the vet package: a repository, a value object, a thin controller, and a template. No existing Java source is modified.
